correctness.rationale: The exact face covering X=union_i(E_i*join_{j!=i}D_j) has all multiple intersections K and null inclusions K->X_i. Iterated homotopy pushouts give an integral wedge of r-spheres and the stated multiplicity; oriented simplicial Lefschetz trace and an exact all-invariant-face enumerator give the full automorphism formula. The all-two-vertex lattice follows from the integral relative long exact sequence. A standalone independent implementation checks 2448 complete automorphisms and eight finite patterns over two primes; this is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the closed all-part-size sphere multiplicity together with a fully evaluated rational wreath-product homology character, including permutations of equal-sized parts, and its integral all-two-vertex augmentation-lattice consequence. Selvaraja and Kim–Lew prove general matroid/tolerance structural and Leray bounds; Moci–Pezzoli prove general equivariant matroid methods. None of the materially inspected specific theorems or indexed comparison claims evaluates this particular automorphism character or the signed integral special case. The qualitative sphere-wedge statement is expressly not claimed new. Unindexed equivalents and derivations from a general matroid framework are recorded as residual risks.
residual_risks: General equivariant matroid theorems may yield an equivalent character after an independently nontrivial specialization; no broad priority guarantee is made.

value.rationale: This is an explicit character for every element of a natural full wreath-product automorphism group, not just a rank or a generic Leray bound. It determines rational quotient Betti dimensions under arbitrary subgroups, and the all-two special case identifies a nontrivial canonical integral signed augmentation lattice. The result addresses a literature-led topological calculation for a natural entire family of one-step matroid elongations. It neither claims general matroid homotopy as original nor depends on an arbitrary small finite table.
